scope: ZF plus countable choice, R_r=Z[x_1^±1,...,x_r^±1] for every finite r and the explicitly enumerated mixed polynomial/Laurent rings, quotients and localizations used in their proof.
verdict: Pass at this exact scope. The supplement supplies a CC proof of K0(R_r)=Z[R_r], K1(R_r)=C2 plus Z^r, and the stated reduced-K0/Whitehead vanishing, when combined with the preserved independently reviewed finite algebra.
checks: A module with a specified countable generating list over an enumerated ring has an explicit enumeration by finite combinations. Submodule enumerations can be obtained by replacing nonmember entries by zero; no simultaneous choice of fresh enumerations is required.

The omega filtration proof for subgroups of countably free Z-modules uses least-coded lifts at each finite-coordinate stage and yields a specified countable basis, without well-ordering an arbitrary set.

Countably free modules really are projective under CC against arbitrary surjections: the countable family of nonempty fibers may consist of arbitrary sets. Summand projectivity and countably generated projective free-splitting therefore have their genuine global lifting meanings.

The polynomial induced exact sequence, finite chain-map lifts and finite mapping cone raise the countably generated projective resolution bound by one. Localization at an explicitly countable multiplicative set preserves enumeration and the bound. Induction for each finite r uses finite stages, not an unspecified dependent-choice iteration.

Noetherianity supplies finite free syzygies. Finite Schanuel comparison with the bounded countable projective resolution proves the final finite kernel projective. For the decreasing kernel bound, K+Q0=L+P with Q0,P projective permits resolving L+P and splitting the lifted Q0 off degree zero; no general unproved direct-summand dimension assertion or unrestricted Ext is necessary.

Noetherian quotient induction has no DC gap: every ideal has a least finite generating code. If no maximal counterexample ideal existed, recursion choosing the least-coded strict successor would give an ascending chain; its finitely generated union forces stabilization.

Nil resolutions remain countable and finite. For the H-to-Nil_P periodic argument, choose even 2q beyond a finite resolution length, repeat the two-periodic projective sequence, and compare with the zero-padded finite resolution by Schanuel. The 2qth syzygy M is then a direct summand of a projective. No Ext computation against arbitrary target modules is needed.

Remaining stabilization, finite presentation lifts, complements, Higman and four-block manipulations are finite constructions. Uniqueness of the resulting Grothendieck-group class avoids any simultaneous selection of one resolution for every module.
